title: SCIM probabilistic retry gating & transactional group reconciliation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our current SCIM deprovisioning flow can trigger large, synchronized retry storms during tenant-wide user/group changes (e.g., when an IdP sends a bulk deprovision event). That leads to transient DB contention, inflated error budgets, and gaps in audit sequencing. Goal: Implement a resilient provisioning/deprovisioning workflow that provides transactional clarity for group membership reconciliation and uses a probabilistic retry gating + circuit-breaker to avoid thundering-herd behavior while preserving eventual consistency and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: System performs group membership reconciliation using a lightweight transaction token so partial updates are detectable and reversible
Deprovisioning spikes do not exceed configured concurrency thresholds for any single tenant (soft limit enforced by gating)
Retry behavior follows probabilistic backoff with tenant-aware jitter and a per-tenant circuit-breaker that opens on sustained error rates
All SCIM user/group changes are emitted to the audit log with monotonically increasing sequence IDs and include deprovisioning windows for forensic queries
End-to-end integration tests cover bulk deprovision, intermittent downstream errors, and recovery paths without creating duplicate side-effects
Operational dashboards surface: active gates, circuit-breaker state by tenant, retry queue depth, and deprovision latency percentiles
implementation_plan: Design a reconciliation token model: each tenant reconciliation run assigns a reconciliation_id and per-group sequence numbers to detect partial application
Introduce a probabilistic retry gate service that accepts a tenant_id and desired concurrency; returns an allow/deny with jittered retry window
Add a per-tenant circuit-breaker that trips on configurable error-rate thresholds and transitions through CLOSE -> HALF_OPEN -> OPEN with exponential cool-down
Modify SCIM worker: write reconciliation metadata (reconciliation_id, seq_no, expected_size) in a lightweight metadata table before applying changes; use idempotency keys for each user/group op
Emit audit events for every state transition (requested -> in_progress -> applied -> tombstoned) with sequence ID and reconciliation_id
Add a rollback path for partially-applied reconciliations that can be invoked by a maintenance job if a reconciliation is abandoned after TTL
Create a migration to backfill reconciliation_id for active tenants over a low-traffic window
Instrument metrics and traces for gating decisions, apply latencies, retry attempts, and circuit-breaker state
testing_plan: Unit tests for reconciliation token generation and idempotency key handling
Load tests that simulate an IdP pushing 100k user deletes across 500 tenants to measure gating effectiveness
Chaos tests: flip downstream DB errors mid-reconciliation to validate rollback and retry behaviors
Integration tests exercising audit sequencing guarantees and queries for event ordering
Regression tests to ensure no increase in API error rates for non-affected tenants
monitoring_and_rollout: Canary rollout to 5% of tenants during off-peak hours with feature flag
Monitor metrics: per-tenant active_gates, retry_attempts_per_minute, deprovision_50/95/99 latency, audit_event_sequence_gaps
Auto-rollback trigger: sustained increase >10% in deprovision latency P95 or >2% rise in 5m error rate for canary tenants
Post-rollout: 72h observation window and a postmortem if any customer-facing incidents occur
Operational runbook for opening a manual maintenance window and invoking the reconciliation rollback job
updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed. Prototype of reconciliation_id table and idempotency keys works locally. Found race with concurrent group-add and group-remove events; mitigation: per-group seq_no enforcement.

2025-02-18: Design review with SRE and Security. Decided to use tenant-scoped circuit-breakers and expose state in the Console for operators. Security requested immutable audit event signatures — added to scope.
2025-02-25: Implemented probabilistic gate service (alpha). Gate supports tenant weights for enterprise tenants to bypass gating during SLA windows.
2025-03-01: Integration tests added for audit sequencing. Discovered edge-case where reconciliation TTL expired during network partition — added TTL extension touched by gate heartbeat.

2025-03-04: First canary deploy to internal-staging with 8 tenants. Observed 40% reduction in retry spikes and no sequence gaps. Next: extend canary to external beta tenants and schedule security review sign-off. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/6543
